title: 107. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Distinguishing Direct and Inverse Proportion
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Recognizing Direct Proportion from a Description
questions.learningObjective: Identify a direct proportion relationship from a verbal description.
questions.question: When one quantity increases, the other quantity increases at a constant ratio. This describes which type of relationship?
questions.explanation: In a direct proportion, the two quantities increase or decrease together and their ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) is constant. This matches the description, so the relationship is a direct proportion. Inverse proportion would preserve a product rather than the constant ratio stated in the question.
questions.hint: Decide whether a ratio or a product stays constant.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret how positive variables change when their product is fixed.
questions.question: Two positive quantities satisfy \(xy=36\). As \(x\) increases, which statement describes \(y\)?

options.label: A
options.text: It decreases so that the product remains \(36\).

options.label: B
options.text: It increases at a fixed ratio to the new value of the first quantity.

questions.explanation: A fixed positive product gives an inverse proportion. Increasing one factor requires decreasing the other. Increasing both factors cannot preserve that positive product.
questions.hint: Look for the defining invariant rather than only whether the quantities increase.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table represents direct or inverse proportion.
questions.question:
The table shows a relationship between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 6 & 12 & 18
\end{array}
\]
Which type of proportion does the table represent?
questions.explanation: Check the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\). For the columns, \(\frac{6}{2}=3\), \(\frac{12}{4}=3\), and \(\frac{18}{6}=3\). The ratio is constant, so the relationship is a direct proportion. The inverse alternative would require a constant product, but the products \(2\times 6=12\), \(4\times 12=48\), and \(6\times 18=108\) differ.
questions.hint: Test both a ratio and a product using the available pairs.

questions.concept: Identifying Direct Proportion from an Equation
questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation that represents a direct proportion.
questions.question: Which equation represents a direct proportion between \(x\) and \(y\)?
questions.explanation: In a direct proportion, the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\) is constant, so \(y=kx\). The equation \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) represents inverse proportion.
questions.hint: Decide whether a ratio or a product stays constant.

questions.concept: Distinguishing Proportion in a Work Context
questions.learningObjective: Identify whether a worker-time relationship is direct or inverse proportion.
questions.question: For a fixed amount of work, identical workers each work at the same constant rate without interfering with each other. Therefore, as the number of workers increases, the time needed decreases. This relationship is:
questions.explanation: Each worker has the same constant rate. For fixed work, the number of workers multiplied by the duration stays constant, so the quantities are inversely proportional. Direct proportion would make more workers take more time at the same rate.
questions.hint: Look for the defining invariant rather than only whether the quantities increase.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table represents direct or inverse proportion.
questions.question:
The table shows a relationship between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 2 & 4 & 8\\
\hline
y & 12 & 6 & 3
\end{array}
\]
Which type of proportion does the table represent?
questions.explanation: Check the product \(xy\). For the columns, \(2\times 12=24\), \(4\times 6=24\), and \(8\times 3=24\). The product is constant, so the relationship is an inverse proportion. The direct alternative would require a constant ratio, but \(\frac{12}{2}=6\), \(\frac{6}{4}=1.5\), and \(\frac{3}{8}=0.375\) differ.
questions.hint: Test both a ratio and a product using the available pairs.

questions.learningObjective: Identify direct proportion from the shape of its graph.
questions.question: A graph of a relationship between \(x\) and \(y\) is a nonvertical straight line with nonzero slope that passes through the origin. Which type of proportion does this graph represent?
questions.explanation: The graph of a direct proportion \(y=kx\) is a straight line passing through the origin. An inverse proportion graph is not a straight line through the origin.
questions.hint: Decide whether a ratio or a product stays constant.

questions.concept: Identifying Inverse Proportion from an Equation
questions.learningObjective: Identify inverse proportion from an equation in product form.
questions.question: The relationship between \(x\) and \(y\) is given by \(xy=24\). Which type of proportion does this represent?
questions.explanation: The equation \(xy=24\) means the product of \(x\) and \(y\) is constant. A constant product is the defining condition of inverse proportion. The direct alternative requires a constant quotient, whereas the stem fixes the product; solving gives \(y=\frac{24}{x}\).
questions.hint: Look for the defining invariant rather than only whether the quantities increase.

questions.concept: Distinguishing Proportion in a Cost Context
questions.learningObjective: Identify direct proportion in a unit-cost relationship.
questions.question: If the cost per item is fixed, the total cost is related to the number of items by:
questions.explanation: With a fixed price per item, total cost equals unit price multiplied by item count. The cost-to-count ratio stays constant, giving direct proportion. Inverse proportion would make the total decrease when the count increases.
questions.hint: Decide whether a ratio or a product stays constant.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table represents direct or inverse proportion.
questions.question:
The table shows a relationship between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 1 & 2 & 4\\
\hline
y & 8 & 4 & 2
\end{array}
\]
Which type of proportion does the table represent?
questions.explanation: Check the product \(xy\). For the columns, \(1\times 8=8\), \(2\times 4=8\), and \(4\times 2=8\). The product is constant, so the table represents an inverse proportion. The direct alternative would require a constant ratio, but \(\frac{8}{1}=8\), \(\frac{4}{2}=2\), and \(\frac{2}{4}=0.5\) differ.
questions.hint: Decide whether a ratio or a product stays constant.
